title: Allah bought what He already gave you, and paid Paradise.
subtitle: The sale every believer carries

row.title: Allah
sub: who gave them in the first place

key.label: What it says about your worth

row.title: He raised the price
sub: bought you and raised your worth

then: In the setting of Tabuk, Allah describes a sale: the believers' lives and wealth for Paradise. Ibn Kathir calls it {reward}His favor and generosity{/reward}, since He accepts as payment what He already owns. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: {reward}Allah bought them and raised their worth.{/reward}
now: Shimr bin Atiyyah said every Muslim has a sale on their neck, to fulfill or leave unfinished. Yours might be the hours you give your sick mother, the salary you share, the energy you spend on what Allah loves. {idea}Every bit of it is part of the deal.{/idea}
old: What I give up for Allah leaves me poorer.
new: Allah takes what He gave me and pays me Paradise for it.
try: Choose one thing you will spend today purely for Allah: an hour, a sum, an effort.

title: Who the buyers are: nine plain qualities.
subtitle: The people of the sale described
then: Ibn Kathir says this is {idea}the description of the believers{/idea} from whom Allah bought their souls and wealth. They repent, worship, praise, and fast, which he says is the meaning of {idea}as-sa'ihun{/idea} here. They pray, guide others to good, and keep Allah's limits, so they worship their Lord and advise His creation.
now: You read a list like this and feel far from it. Look at the first word: {idea}those who repent.{/idea} Not those who never fall. The list starts where you are when you turn back, and grows from there.
old: These qualities belong to people far better than me.
new: The list starts with turning back, which I can do today.
try: Pick one quality from the list and practice it once today, starting with a repentance.

title: Even love for family has a limit set by Allah.
subtitle: The Prophet's ﷺ grief for his uncle and his mother
then: When his uncle Abu Talib was dying, the Prophet ﷺ begged him: {reward}O uncle, say La ilaha illallah{/reward}, and I will plead for you. Abu Talib chose his fathers' religion. Visiting his own mother's grave, the Prophet ﷺ was {trap}more tearful than they had ever seen him.{/trap} Allah said: you do not guide whom you love.
now: Your brother has drifted far. Your father mocks your prayer. You love them and it hurts. {idea}Even the Prophet ﷺ could not make the heart of the one he loved most turn.{/idea} Keep loving, keep praying for them while they live, and leave the heart to Allah.
old: If I love them enough, I can bring them to faith.
new: I can love, invite, and pray, but guidance belongs to Allah.
try: Make a sincere dua today for one relative who is far from faith, while they are alive.

title: Ibrahim kept a promise to his father, then let go.
subtitle: A tender heart and a clear line
then: When the Prophet ﷺ mentioned that Ibrahim had prayed for his father, this verse explained it: {idea}it was a promise he had made.{/idea} Ibn Abbas said Ibrahim kept praying for him until he died, then dissociated. Ibn Masud said awwah means {reward}one who calls on Allah constantly.{/reward}
now: You made a promise to someone you love, and you keep it as long as you honestly can. When a line has to be drawn, you draw it without hardness. {idea}Ibrahim shows that tenderness and firmness can live in the same heart.{/idea}
old: Drawing a line with family means I stopped caring.
new: I can keep my promises, accept Allah's limits, and stay gentle.
try: Turn to Allah in a short private dua today, like Ibrahim the awwah, about someone you love.

title: Allah makes clear what to avoid before He holds you to it.
subtitle: Guidance comes before accountability
then: Ibn Abbas said some believers used to pray for relatives who died opposing Allah, until the verses before came. Ibn Jarir explained: {reward}before He informs you an action is not allowed{/reward}, you have not disobeyed Him. Mujahid said it is also a general call: {idea}beware of disobeying Him and be eager to obey.{/idea}
now: You learn something new about your faith and feel a wave of panic about all the years you did not know. The verse is a calm hand on your shoulder. {reward}Allah is just.{/reward} What matters is what you do now that you know.
old: I am guilty for everything I did before I knew better.
new: Allah makes things clear first; what I do after knowing is what counts.
try: Act on one thing you learned recently, without dwelling on the years before.

title: He owns the heavens and earth, gives life and death.
subtitle: No protector or helper besides Him
then: After the verses about praying for relatives, this verse turns the believers back to Allah alone. Ibn Jarir said it is {idea}a command to trust in Allah's aid{/idea}, for He owns the heavens and earth, and {reward}not to fear His enemies.{/reward}
now: Your visa is stuck, the job offer depends on one person's signature, a test result is due Thursday. You keep refreshing your inbox as if someone there holds your fate. {idea}Everything in that inbox belongs to Allah too.{/idea}
old: My future depends on the people who control my situation.
new: Allah owns every situation and is the only true protector.
try: When you check on something you are anxious about today, say first: Allah is enough for me.

title: Forgiven in the hour of hardship.
subtitle: When even faithful hearts almost wavered
then: Tabuk came in a year of {trap}little rain, intense heat, and scarce water.{/trap} Qatadah said two men would share one date. Umar recalled thirst so hard they thought their necks would break, until the Prophet ﷺ raised his hands and {reward}rain fell on their camp.{/reward} Ibn Jarir said some hearts nearly doubted from the hardship.
now: A long illness, a year of rejections, a stretch where your prayers feel like they hit the ceiling. Somewhere in there a quiet voice asks if any of this is real. {reward}The verse says Allah saw that hour, and forgave, and held them steady.{/reward}
old: If my faith shook during hard times, it was never real.
new: Allah knows how hard the hour is and turns to the hearts that nearly slipped.
try: In your next hard moment, say: O Allah, keep my heart firm.

title: The earth closed in on them, and only He was refuge.
subtitle: Kab bin Malik and fifty nights

row.title: "Be happy, Kab!"
sub: the best day of his life

then: Kab said he was never wealthier than the year he stayed behind. He kept delaying, telling himself {trap}I can do that if I want{/trap}, until the army had gone. Over eighty men gave excuses; he told the Prophet ﷺ the truth. After fifty nights of silence, a voice cried from a mountain: {reward}Kab, be happy!{/reward}
now: You missed the moment by putting it off one day at a time. Now the room has gone cold, people avoid your eyes, and your own house feels strange. {idea}Kab did not run to the outside offer or a better story.{/idea} He waited on Allah, and the relief came.
old: When everyone turns away, I need a way out on my own.
new: When everything closes in, the only real refuge is Allah Himself.
try: If something heavy is pressing on you, take it to Allah in a long sujood tonight.

title: Fear Allah, and be with the truthful.
subtitle: The lesson of Kab's honesty

key.label: What Kab called his greatest blessing

then: After his repentance was accepted, Kab said Allah saved him {idea}for telling the truth{/idea}, and vowed to speak only the truth for life. Ibn Kathir quotes the Prophet ﷺ: {reward}truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise.{/reward} A person keeps striving for truth until written as truthful.
now: Your boss asks why the report is late. Your mother asks where you were. A small lie would be so smooth. {idea}Kab had the words for the perfect excuse too.{/idea} The verse asks you to stand with the truthful, even when it costs.
old: A small lie is easier on everyone.
new: The truth, even when it costs, is what saves me.
try: Tell the plain truth today in one moment where a small lie would be easier.

title: Every thirst, every tired step, is written down.
subtitle: No effort for Allah is wasted
then: Ibn Kathir says those around Madinah who stayed back from Tabuk {trap}preferred to preserve themselves{/trap} over sharing the Prophet's ﷺ hardship. They lost the reward written for those who went: every thirst, every fatigue, every hunger, even things {reward}not under their control{/reward}, recorded as good deeds.
now: The night shift where you stayed patient. The tired walk to the masjid in the rain. The hunger of a long fast at work. You think none of it counts because nothing big came of it. {reward}Allah does not let the reward of those who do good be lost.{/reward}
old: The hard parts of doing good are just the price, not the reward.
new: Every bit of tiredness for Allah's sake is written as a good deed.
try: When you feel tired doing something good today, quietly intend it for Allah.
